targets.name: Erdos9.erdos_9.variants.infinite
targets.plain: The set is known to be infinite. In [Er77c] Erdős credits Schinzel with proving that there are infinitely many odd integers not of this form, but gives no reference. [Er77c] Erdős, P., _Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III._.

targets.name: Erdos9.erdos_9
targets.plain: Is the upper density of the set of odd numbers that cannot be expressed as a prime plus two powers of 2 positive?

targets.name: Erdos23.erdos_23.variants.n1
targets.plain: Every triangle-free graph on 5 vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most 1 edge. This is the n = 1 case of Erdős Problem 23.
targets.statement: : ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)), H ≤ G ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ 1

targets.name: Erdos23.erdos_23.variants.n5
targets.plain: Every triangle-free graph on 25 vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most 25 edges. This is the n = 5 case of Erdős Problem 23. It follows from the high-density range of Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky together with McKay's complete catalogue of the 23-vertex extremal graphs for bipartization of triangle-free graphs.
targets.statement: : ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), H ≤ G ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ 25

targets.name: Erdos23.erdos_23.variants.n5_tight
targets.plain: There exists a triangle-free graph on 25 vertices such that at least 25 edges must be removed to make it bipartite. The balanced blow-up of C_5 with five parts of size 5 witnesses this.
targets.statement: : ∃ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), G.CliqueFree 3 ∧ ∀ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), H ≤ G → H.IsBipartite → 25 ≤ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card

targets.name: Erdos23.blowupC5_tight
targets.plain: The blow-up of C_5 shows that the bound n^2 in Erdős Problem 23 is tight: any bipartite subgraph must omit at least n^2 edges.
targets.statement: (n : ℕ) (_hn : 0 < n) (H : SimpleGraph (ZMod 5 × Fin n)) (hH : H ≤ blowupC5 n) (hBip : H.IsBipartite) : n ^ 2 ≤ ((blowupC5 n).edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card

targets.name: Erdos23.erdos_23
targets.plain: Can every triangle-free graph on 5n vertices be made bipartite by deleting at most n^2 edges?
targets.statement: : ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V], Fintype.card V = 5 * n → ∀ (G : SimpleGraph V), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ (H : SimpleGraph V), H ≤ G ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ n^2

targets.name: Erdos1052.erdos_1052
targets.plain: Are there only finitely many unitary perfect numbers?

targets.name: Erdos1052.even_of_isUnitaryPerfect
targets.plain: All unitary perfect numbers are even. Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof.

targets.name: Erdos1059.erdos_1059
targets.plain: Are there infinitely many primes p such that p - k! is composite for each k such that 1 ≤ k! < p?

targets.name: Erdos1142.erdos_1142
targets.plain: Are there infinitely many n > 2 such that n - 2^k is prime for all k ≥ 1 with 2^k < n? The only known such n are 4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105 (OEIS [A039669](https://oeis.org/A039669)).

targets.name: Erdos1142.erdos_1142.variants.mientka_weitzenkamp
targets.plain: Mientka and Weitzenkamp [MiWe69] proved that the only n ≤ 2^44 such that n > 2 and n - 2^k is prime for all k ≥ 1 with 2^k < n are 4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105.
